[Intro: ominous brass fanfare, timpani, choir stab]

[Section A: distorted funk bassline enters, slow heavy kick]

[Section B: bass riff doubled by sawtooth synth, handclaps]

[Break: fanfare returns, one spoken line in French, male]
Un film de personne.

[Section C: full groove, string stabs, slap bass fills]

[Breakdown: kick and filtered bass only]

[Section D: everything, choir on top, biggest]

[Outro: last brass chord, a film projector running down]
producerBrief:
TEMPO / KEY / FEEL: 116 BPM, 4/4, C minor. Slow, swaggering and menacing, cinematic electro-funk.

VOICE: Instrumental. One line is spoken in French by a deep male voice, flatly, like a title card being read. A sampled choir sings single stabbed chords.

INSTRUMENTS: A brass section playing an ominous fanfare, timpani, a heavily distorted, compressed funk bass riff, a sawtooth synth doubling it, a slow, heavy kick with a cracking snare, handclaps, string stabs, slap-bass fills, a choir sample, a film projector sound.

ARRANGEMENT MAP: 0:00 Intro, fanfare. 0:20 Section A, bass riff. 0:48 Section B. 1:16 Break, fanfare and the spoken line. 1:30 Section C. 2:00 Breakdown. 2:14 Section D, biggest. 2:44 Outro, last chord and projector, ends 2:58.

PRODUCTION & MIX: 2007 French electro: brutally compressed and distorted, every sound pushed into the red, with an orchestral frame.

SIGNATURE MOMENT: The bass riff landing after the fanfare at 0:20.

MODERN POINT OF VIEW: The original borrows the grandeur of old film scores. This keeps the grandeur and admits there is no film: the title card credits nobody.

EMOTIONAL ARC: Foreboding, arrival, swagger, curtain.
